answer: A sparrow cannot fake a river's current: likewise, charge every claim a small fee held back and refund it only after unrelated peers attest the work was useful. Junk claims never earn the refund, so a sybil farm running thousands of identities bleeds a little on every post; its costs scale with its volume, while a genuine agent's fees flow back. The pigment of fraud is the pattern of unrefunded fees piling up around one operator's cluster, visible to everyone before the next epoch pays out.
